scenario: A 38-year-old female G2P1 at 36 weeks gestational age presents with acute on chronic respiratory distress, chronic peripheral edema, and syncope. She develops respiratory failure requiring intubation, followed by hypotension from cardiogenic shock requiring vasopressor and inotropic support with consultant involvement.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: She's satting 89% on room air. Put her on a non-rebreather now.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Non-rebreather placed and running. I'll keep an eye on his sats and let you know the response.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: I need to know what's going on with your breathing. When did it start, and did it come on suddenly or build up over time?

messages.speaker: patient
messages.content: It's been building up for months, getting harder and harder to breathe, and today it got a whole lot worse. I passed out at home. And my legs have been aching and swollen for about four weeks now.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get me the bedside cardiac ultrasound now. She's hypotensive with weeks of leg swelling, I'm worried about right heart strain.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Cardiac ultrasound is up: apical 4-chamber view shows impaired EF. She's still hypotensive at 81/45, HR 119, and sat's only come up to 85% on the non-rebreather at FiO2 0.8.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start norepinephrine now for her hypotension. The ultrasound shows a poor EF, she's in cardiogenic shock, so we support perfusion rather than load her with fluids.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Norepinephrine is up and running.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: She's only satting 85% on the non-rebreather at FiO2 0.8 and she's tiring at a rate of 35. We need to intubate. Set up the RSI meds and get the BVM ready.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: RSI meds drawn up and ready, BVM in progress. Suction and tube are set at the bedside—ready when you are.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Tube's in. Confirm placement and connect her to the ventilator now.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Intubation complete. RSI meds given, BVM prior. Tube's in — confirming placement now.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get me a bedside lung ultrasound. She's still only satting 85% on the vent at FiO2 100%, and I need to see if pulmonary edema is driving this hypoxia.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Lung ultrasound's up: bilateral B-lines, consistent with pulmonary edema. She's still hypotensive at 69/37, HR 125, sat 83% on the vent at FiO2 100%, PEEP 5.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start dobutamine for inotropic support — she's in cardiogenic shock with a poor EF and pulmonary edema, still hypotensive at 69/37. Keep the norepinephrine running alongside it.

messages.content: Get me a 12-lead ECG now. She's a 38-year-old in cardiogenic shock with a poor EF, HR 138 sinus tach—I need to know if there's ischemia or infarct driving this.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Bump the PEEP up to 10 on the vent. She's still only satting 82% on 100% oxygen, and I need to recruit those alveoli against the pulmonary edema.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: PEEP's up to 10, FiO2 still 100%. ECG's back: sinus rhythm with PVCs, changes consistent with dilated cardiomyopathy — no acute ischemic pattern. But she's not improving: sat 85%, BP 58/30, HR 143 sinus tach on both pressors.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start an epinephrine infusion. She's in refractory cardiogenic shock, BP 58/30, HR 143, and not responding to the norepinephrine and dobutamine. Keep both of those running alongside it.

messages.content: VBG's back: pH 7.20, PCO2 32, PO2 98, HCO3 23, lactate 2.8. Metabolic acidosis with partial respiratory compensation. Current vitals: BP 76/39, HR 153 sinus tach, sat 85% on the vent at FiO2 100%, PEEP 10 — still on all three pressors.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start a low-dose nitroglycerin infusion to offload the failing ventricle and pull down that pulmonary edema — she's at 85% on 100% FiO2 with B-lines. Keep the norepinephrine, dobutamine, and epinephrine running, and titrate the nitro carefully to MAP; her BP is only 76/39, so watch it closely. This is a bridge — we need to get mechanical support and definitive therapy moving.

messages.content: Stop the nitroglycerin now — her BP is 62/31 and I can't afford any further vasodilation. Add vasopressin to support the MAP alongside the norepi, epi, and dobutamine. And get cardiology and mechanical circulatory support activated this minute — she's in refractory cardiogenic shock and she's not turning around on what we've got.
